\section[a lareira]{a lareira — fireplace}

\label{lesson:PT-C532-lareira}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for (electric) drill, then the Portuguese for pliers.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a lareira}
\textbf{a lareira} — \textquotedblleft{}fireplace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No inverno, jantamos ao pé da lareira.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In winter, we have dinner by the fireplace.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Acender a lareira} — to light the fire.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lareira} is built on \emph{lar} \textquotedblleft{}hearth, home\textquotedblright{}, which comes from Latin \emph{lar}, the god of the household (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a lareira}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a lareira}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a lareira}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for (electric) drill, then the Portuguese for pliers, then say \emph{a lareira} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a lareira mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fireplace\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a almofada]{a almofada — cushion; pillow}

\label{lesson:PT-C532-almofada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for pliers, then the Portuguese for fireplace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a almofada}
\textbf{a almofada} — \textquotedblleft{}cushion; pillow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O sofá tem muitas almofadas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The sofa has lots of cushions.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal also the pillow on a bed; in Brazil that is \emph{o travesseiro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{almofada} comes, through Andalusian Arabic, from Arabic \emph{mikhadda} \textquotedblleft{}a cushion\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a almofada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a almofada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a almofada}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for pliers, then the Portuguese for fireplace, then say \emph{a almofada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a almofada mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Cushion; pillow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a estante]{a estante — bookcase}

\label{lesson:PT-C532-estante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for fireplace, then the Portuguese for cushion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a estante}
\textbf{a estante} — \textquotedblleft{}bookcase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A estante da sala está cheia de livros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bookcase in the living room is full of books.}
\end{quote}

A single shelf is \emph{uma prateleira}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{estante} comes from Latin \emph{stāns} \textquotedblleft{}standing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{stāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}: a piece of furniture that stands up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a estante}

\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[o soalho]{o soalho — wooden floor, floorboards}

\label{lesson:PT-C532-soalho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for cushion, then the Portuguese for bookcase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o soalho}
\textbf{o soalho} — \textquotedblleft{}wooden floor, floorboards\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O soalho da casa antiga range.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The wooden floor in the old house creaks.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil, \emph{o assoalho}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{soalho} is usually traced to a form built on Latin \emph{solum} \textquotedblleft{}ground, floor\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a decoração]{a decoração — decoration, decor}

\label{lesson:PT-C532-decoracao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for bookcase, then the Portuguese for wooden floor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a decoração}
\textbf{a decoração} — \textquotedblleft{}decoration, decor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Gosto muito da decoração da tua casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I really like the decor of your house.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{decorar} in the sense \textquotedblleft{}to decorate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{decoração} is built on \emph{decorar} \textquotedblleft{}to decorate\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{decorāre} \textquotedblleft{}to adorn\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{decus} \textquotedblleft{}ornament, grace\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a decoração}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for bookcase, then the Portuguese for wooden floor, then say \emph{a decoração} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\label{lesson:PT-R532-revisao-531-532}



\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to repair, to hang, to hammer, (electric) drill, pliers
  \item fireplace, cushion, bookcase, wooden floor, decoration

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To repair? (\textbf{consertar}.) To hang? (\textbf{pendurar}.) To hammer? (\textbf{martelar}.) (electric) drill? (\textbf{o berbequim}.) Pliers? (\textbf{o alicate}.) Fireplace? (\textbf{a lareira}.) Cushion? (\textbf{a almofada}.) Bookcase? (\textbf{a estante}.) Wooden floor? (\textbf{o soalho}.) Decoration? (\textbf{a decoração}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
